sections.h2: What should I know before selling a house in Georgetown, KY?
sections.html:
Georgetown owners can list, sell on their own or take a cash offer, and Scott County's offices handle the tax bill, the deed and the delinquent-tax process that matters if payments have lapsed. Georgetown is the Scott County seat and the sixth-largest city in Kentucky, with 37,086 residents in 2020 and an estimated 40,883 on July 1, 2025.

It is also the highest-priced of the four cities in this group, with the largest households and the highest income, which sets the tone for the local market.

sections.h2: Where is Georgetown and how did it grow?
sections.html:
Georgetown lies north of Lexington in the Bluegrass region. Interstate 75 passes east of downtown with exits 125, 126, 127 and 129, putting downtown Lexington 16 miles south and Cincinnati 69 miles north. U.S. 25 runs through the center, U.S. 62 forms a bypass along the south and east, and U.S. 460 leads 18 miles west to Frankfort.

Baptist minister Elijah Craig brought a congregation here in 1782 and founded a settlement called Lebanon, incorporated in 1784 around the Royal Spring. The name changed to George Town for George Washington in 1790, Scott County was formed in 1792, and the spelling became Georgetown in 1846. After the Civil War the town became a rail hub, and the line from Frankfort carried much of the region's bourbon toward the Ohio River.

The modern city dates from Toyota's decision in 1985 to build a plant here. Toyota Motor Manufacturing Kentucky opened in 1988 and builds the Camry, Lexus ES and RAV4. The city's 2018 financial report listed Toyota as the largest employer at 10,019 people, ahead of Scott County Schools at 1,219 and Adient at 743. The population climbed from 18,080 in 2000 to 29,098 in 2010 and 37,086 in 2020.

The climate is humid subtropical, with average July highs near 86 degrees, January lows near 25 and about 45 inches of precipitation a year. Gutters, roof drainage and basement moisture are the weather-related items worth checking before a showing.

sections.h2: Which schools and neighborhoods serve Georgetown homes?
sections.html:
Scott County Schools runs the public schools for Georgetown. The district has nine elementary schools, three middle schools and two high schools, Scott County High School and Great Crossing High School, which opened in 2019. Elkhorn Crossing School gives some sophomores and juniors a program that blends academics with career training.

  • Georgetown College, a private liberal arts college, is downtown, and the Baptist Seminary of Kentucky is also in the city.
  • The Oxford Historic District in the business section and Ward Hall, a Greek Revival house just outside the city, are on the National Register of Historic Places.
  • Private options include St. John, Providence Christian Academy and Keystone Montessori.

sections.h2: How does Scott County collect property tax and what happens if bills go unpaid?
sections.html:
The Scott County Sheriff collects tax for 28 districts, and bills are normally mailed on November 1. The sheriff does not set values: questions about assessment go to the Scott County PVA, on the second floor of the courthouse at 101 East Main Street, or by phone at (502) 863-7885.

The county clerk's published timeline for bills left unpaid is a useful warning for anyone behind on taxes before a sale:

  • April 15: delinquent certificates move to the County Clerk's office.
  • May and June: the County Attorney mails two notices, and the first offers a payment agreement to eligible owners.
  • June 30: last day to enter a payment agreement.
  • July 1: advertising costs are added to bills still unpaid, which are published in the newspaper.
  • Late summer: payment is due by a cutoff before the annual delinquent tax sale.

The clerk accepts cash, cashier's checks, money orders and cards, with a 2.75% vendor fee on cards. State rules add a 10% penalty and a sheriff's add-on fee when a bill transfers, plus interest of 1% a month. If you owe delinquent tax, ask the clerk for a payoff figure before you set a closing date, because a title company will require it.

sections.h2: What does a Georgetown seller pay in transfer tax and where is the deed recorded?
sections.html:
Kentucky charges the seller fifty cents for every $500 of value in the deed or fraction of it. At the Census median of $265,400 that is about $265.50, collected by the Scott County Clerk at 101 East Main Street when the deed is recorded. The clerk's office is open Monday through Friday, 8:30 a.m. to 4:30 p.m., and takes calls at (502) 863-7875.

A homeowner age 65 or older, or totally disabled, may qualify for the state homestead exemption of $49,100, applied through the Scott County PVA. A buyer must apply again after the sale, because the exemption belongs to the owner and not the house.

sections.h2: Who handles permits and zoning questions in Georgetown?
sections.html:
The City of Georgetown handles building permits for both the city and Scott County, from the Building Inspection Department at 125 West Clinton Street. Zoning, plats and floodplain information come from the Georgetown-Scott County Planning Commission, which offers a zoning map and a plat finder on its site and answers at (502) 867-3701.

If you plan to sell a house that you added to or finished a basement in, ask the building department whether permits were closed out. A buyer's title review is simpler when the paperwork matches the house. Ask the planning office whether a short-term rental registration applies if the house has been rented by the night.

sections.h2: Which route works for a Georgetown house?
sections.html:
Before you compare offers, gather these items:

  • The current and prior year tax bills from the sheriff, plus any delinquent certificate from the clerk.
  • A mortgage payoff statement, and the release for any other recorded lien.
  • Permit records from the City of Georgetown for additions or major repairs.
  • Lease copies and tenant contact details if the house is rented.

An agent listing suits a house in good order with time to market it. A private sale needs an attorney for the contract and deed. A cash offer fits houses with deferred repairs, tenants, delinquent taxes or an estate to settle. Compare offers by what you net after the mortgage payoff, the transfer tax, prorated property tax and any repair credits.

faqs.q: What is the transfer tax on a Georgetown house sale?
faqs.a: Fifty cents per $500 of value, paid by the seller. On the Census median value of $265,400 it is about $265.50, collected by the Scott County Clerk at recording.

faqs.q: When does Scott County mail property tax bills?
faqs.a: The Scott County Sheriff normally mails them on November 1. The bill lists the due dates, how to avoid penalties and what to do if a mortgage company pays.

faqs.q: What happens to unpaid Georgetown property taxes?
faqs.a: Unpaid bills transfer to the Scott County Clerk around April 15. The County Attorney sends notices in May and June, advertising costs are added July 1, and the bill can be sold at the annual delinquent tax sale.

faqs.q: Who do I call about a Georgetown assessment?
faqs.a: Call the Scott County Property Valuation Administrator at (502) 863-7885. The sheriff collects the tax but does not assess property.

faqs.q: Where do I get a building permit in Georgetown?
faqs.a: Building permits for Georgetown and Scott County come from the City of Georgetown's Building Inspection Department at 125 West Clinton Street. Zoning and plat questions go to the Georgetown-Scott County Planning Commission at (502) 867-3701.
